question: In a referendum, Icelanders rejected the resumption of negotiations on EU accession. Iceland is one of the most developed countries in Europe, it is part of the single market through the EEA, and it is in the Schengen area. Most voters nevertheless opted for cooperation without membership. If a democratic and prosperous European country prefers to remain outside the Union, it is fair to ask whether the problem is not with the EU itself. 1.

Does the Commission regard the result of the Icelandic referendum as a sign that the EU is on the wrong track, given that even a developed European country does not feel that full membership offers enough advantages?
Does the Commission see a link between the result of the referendum and the extent to which legislation and powers are being transferred from Member States to the EU level?
